text.p: Vauxhall, the British car company, has acquired the main advertising rights for an Internet Website about Britain's upcoming election, a company involved in the deal said on Wednesday.
TSMSi, which books advertising space on the Internet and is owned by TSMS, Britain's biggest television advertising sales house, said Vauxhall would use the Website to advertise its Omega car.
The Website, called "Election '97", is being created by Independent Television News (ITN), which provides national and international news for Britain's independent TV companies.
The site -- which goes live on April 1 at http://www.itnelection.co.uk -- will provide news coverage of the May 1 general election.
TSMSi said the advertising deal was booked through Lowe Digital, the digital marketing division of Lowe & Partners UK advertising agency.
Charlie Dobres, marketing and media director of Lowe Digital, said the ITN site was a good place for Omega ads that describe the car as a way to escape stress.
"The ITN site is a great on-line media environment in which to carry through Omega's positioning as an aid to relaxation," he said in a statement from TSMSi.
Vauxhall will run a competition on the Website with prizes which include weekend breaks at a health farm.
"The soothing prizes will be the perfect antidote to election fever," said Dobres.
TSMSi said it expected a lot of Internet users to visit the site. It said it expected "Election '97" to generate a minimum of 500,000 "page impressions".
Vauxhall is owned by General Motors Corp in the United States.
